rules.title: Conventional Commits
rules.text: Write commit messages in Conventional Commits format (feat:, fix:, docs:, refactor:, test:, chore:) and mark breaking changes with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE footer.

rules.title: Small pull requests
rules.text: Keep pull requests small and focused on one change.

rules.title: Imperative commit subjects
rules.text: Write commit subjects in the imperative mood, 72 characters or fewer.

rules.title: No force push
rules.text: Never force-push to shared branches and never rewrite published history.

rules.title: Branch naming
rules.text: Name branches type/short-description, for example feat/add-login.

rules.title: Run checks before commit
rules.text: Run lint, type check and tests before committing.

rules.title: No secrets in commits
rules.text: Never commit secrets, build output or large binaries.

rules.title: Explain the why in PRs
rules.text: Describe motivation, approach and testing in the pull request description.

rules.title: Atomic commits
rules.text: Make each commit one logical change that builds and passes tests.

rules.title: No WIP in shared branches
rules.text: Squash fixup and WIP commits before merging.

rules.title: Link issues
rules.text: Reference the issue or ticket in the commit body or pull request.

rules.title: No history rewrite after push
rules.text: Do not amend or rebase commits that are already pushed to a shared branch.

rules.title: Keep .gitignore current
rules.text: Add build output, local env files and editor files to .gitignore instead of committing them.

rules.title: Review-ready PRs
rules.text: Open pull requests only when CI is green and the diff is self-reviewed.

rules.title: Do not skip hooks
rules.text: Never bypass commit hooks or signing with --no-verify unless explicitly instructed.

rules.title: Explain why in the body
rules.text: Use the commit body to explain why the change was made when it is not obvious.

rules.title: Scoped commit titles
rules.text: Use Conventional Commits with a scope, and keep the subject lowercase and imperative when the project asks for it.

rules.title: Closing keywords in the PR
rules.text: Put closing keywords such as "Fixes #123" in the PR description rather than commit messages, so the issue closes only on merge.

rules.title: No @mentions in commits
rules.text: Do not put @mentions in commit messages. They notify people on every rebase.

rules.title: Keep review history
rules.text: After a PR is open, add new commits for review fixes. Do not amend, squash or rebase pushed commits.

rules.title: Squash fixups into commits
rules.text: Squash review fixes into the commits they correct before merge, so no commit ships known-wrong code followed by a fixup.

rules.title: Every commit builds
rules.text: Make each commit compile and pass tests on its own, and keep fixup commits out of the final history.
